Now, to really understand the NATO story, there's something most coverage leaves out.
Most coverage treats NATO summits as simple gatherings where leaders issued joint statements,
yet the real process involves months of behind-the-scenes bargaining over spending targets
and capability targets before any public announcement. Each member state arrives with national
budget constraints and domestic political calendars that shape what it can promise,
so agreements often emerge as phased commitments rather than immediate spending increases.
The Secretary-General's role is to broker compromises that keep all 32 nations aligned
without forcing any single capital into an untenable position at home.
Knowing this, when headlines announce new defense pledges, readers can check whether the numbers
represent fresh cash or previously planned outlays simply relabelled for the summit.

targets have actually translated into delivered capabilities over subsequent years.
